options: To delete the resource's headers, leaving the body unchanged
To get the API schema in OpenAPI format with a description of all endpoints, parameters and types
To update part of a resource, like PATCH, but without a response body to save traffic
To get only the response headers without the body: check that a resource exists or a file's size
1wre745.explanation: A HEAD response must contain the same headers as a GET on the same resource.

13k4aai.text: What does 409 mean in response to a PATCH with the resource version?
options: The resource was deleted by another user, and the server can't apply changes to it
A state conflict: someone else changed the resource after the client read it
A wrong body format: the version field must be a string, not a number
No permission to change the resource, because the version belongs to another user
13k4aai.explanation: An optimistic locking test: two clients read version 5, the first updates, and the second must get a conflict, not silently overwrite the changes.

y9292j.text: How do ETag and If-None-Match work?
options: The client sends the saved ETag, and if the resource hasn't changed, the server answers 304 without a body
ETag encrypts the response body, and If-None-Match decrypts it on the client
The server always returns 200 with the full body, and If-None-Match only writes the ETag to logs for analytics
If-None-Match creates the resource if there is no such ETag on the server yet, and returns 201
y9292j.explanation: Test: two GETs, the second with If-None-Match, expect 304. After the resource changes, 200 again with a new ETag.

1n54eu.text: What will the server return for a PUT with `If-Match: "v5"` if the current version is already v6?
options: 304 Not Modified
412 Precondition Failed
200, and it overwrites the resource, because PUT always replaces the data
Always 409, because 412 is used only for GET
1n54eu.explanation: If-Match protects against a lost update at the HTTP level. Some APIs use 409 and a version field in the body instead.

options: no-store allows caching the response for a day in the browser, and no-cache forbids any storage and proxy cache
no-cache forbids any caching in the browser, and no-store forbids only intermediate proxies and CDNs from keeping a copy of the response
no-cache allows storing but requires validation with the server before use; no-store forbids storing at all
no-store allows storing but requires validation with the server; no-cache forbids storing at all
1vynmbj.explanation: Responses with a balance or personal data must be no-store. This is worth checking in security tests.

1zxcst.text: Why does a request from the front end fail because of CORS, but work from Postman?
options: The server recognises Postman by its user agent and lets it through without checking Origin
CORS is enforced only by the browser; Postman and curl don't check the Access-Control-* headers
It is a Postman bug: it ignores security settings, so results of tests in it can't be considered reliable
Postman sends a different token and bypasses the Origin check through its own proxy
1zxcst.explanation: That is why CORS configuration is tested from a browser or by checking the headers of the preflight response.

1we67ub.text: When does the browser send a preflight OPTIONS?
options: Only on the first request of a session to a new domain, after which the browser remembers the permission until the tab is closed
Before every GET request to another domain, even a simple one
For cross-origin requests that are not simple: the PUT or DELETE method, an Authorization header, Content-Type application/json
Only for HTTPS requests, because HTTP requests are sent by the browser without a prior check
1we67ub.explanation: A typical bug: the server answers OPTIONS with 401 because it requires a token, while the browser sends the preflight without one.

z0xh2r.text: Why doesn't `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` together with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` work?
options: Only HTTPS is needed: on HTTP the browser ignores Allow-Credentials, and on HTTPS the wildcard works with cookies
The wildcard is allowed only for POST requests, and a GET with cookies requires a list of domains
The browser forbids the wildcard for requests with cookies; the server must return a specific origin
It is a correct configuration, and the problem is always that the client doesn't send cookies
z0xh2r.explanation: A dangerous alternative: reflecting any Origin from the request. Test: a request from an arbitrary Origin must not get permission.

1f9xm8i.text: What does the `Retry-After` header mean in a 429 or 503 response?
options: The token's lifetime in seconds, after which the client must renew it with refresh
How many retries remain before the client is blocked
The processing time of the previous request in seconds
In how many seconds (or at what time) the client should repeat the request
1f9xm8i.explanation: A correct client respects Retry-After instead of retrying immediately in a loop.

18scqim.text: Is the content of a JWT encrypted?
options: Yes, always: the payload is encrypted with the server secret, and without it the content can't be read
Yes, if HTTPS is used: the payload is encrypted together with the traffic and can't be read without the server key
No: the payload is only base64url-encoded and anyone can read it; the signature protects against changes, not against reading
Only the sub field with the user identifier is encrypted, and the rest of the payload is sent as plain text
18scqim.explanation: Passwords and sensitive data are not put in a JWT. The check: decode the token on jwt.io and see what is in it.

wvfj8e.text: How do you test that the backend really verifies the JWT signature?
options: Send the same token twice in a row and check that the second request is rejected
Remove the Content-Type header and check that the server returns 415 instead of 200
Change the payload (for example role to admin) without re-signing and make sure the response is 401
Check the token on jwt.io: if the site shows "Signature Verified", the backend verifies it too
wvfj8e.explanation: More cases: alg none, an expired exp, a token from another environment, a revoked token after logout.

olvmln.text: Why a refresh token if there is an access token?
options: Refresh is needed only for mobile apps, because the browser stores access in a cookie with no expiry limit
It is the same token that is simply renewed on every API request
Access lives briefly and is sent often, refresh lives longer and is used only to get a new access
Refresh replaces the password in mobile apps and lives as long as access
olvmln.explanation: Test cases: an expired access plus a valid refresh gives a new access; a revoked refresh after logout no longer works.

16l8j6m.text: Which OAuth 2.0 flow suits service-to-service integration without a user?
options: Authorization Code with PKCE
Client Credentials
Implicit
Resource Owner Password
16l8j6m.explanation: Authorization Code with PKCE is for SPAs and mobile apps on behalf of a user. The Implicit and Password flows are deprecated.

njmucu.text: What does the HttpOnly flag give a session cookie?
options: The cookie is encrypted by the browser and sent only to the server that set it
The cookie is not sent to other domains and subdomains, even if Domain is set
The cookie is sent only over HTTPS and doesn't end up in unencrypted traffic
JavaScript on the page can't read the cookie, which protects the session from theft via XSS
njmucu.explanation: Secure restricts sending to HTTPS, SameSite protects against CSRF. The check: `document.cookie` in the console must not show the session cookie.

options: SQL injection through cookies, because the browser escapes the value before sending
XSS: the browser forbids JavaScript from reading cookies from other sites
Traffic interception on public Wi-Fi networks, because the cookie is sent only over HTTPS
CSRF: the browser doesn't send the cookie in cross-site requests (Lax allows only navigational GETs)
1s3aqu8.explanation: Test: a form on another domain that makes a POST to your API must not succeed with the user's session.

1of3nbj.text: A user updates their profile and adds `"role": "admin"` to the body. The server saves the role. What is this vulnerability called?
options: CSRF through the profile form
XSS through the role field
Mass assignment (in the OWASP API Top 10: Broken Object Property Level Authorization)
IDOR
1of3nbj.explanation: The server must accept only allowed fields. Test: add internal fields (role, balance, isVerified) to the body and check that they are ignored or give 400.

re2e20.text: What do you check after logout from the API's point of view?
options: That the cookie was removed only on the client, and the login page opened after the redirect
That the login page opened and the cookie was removed in the browser
That the old access and refresh tokens no longer work, and protected endpoints return 401
Nothing: logout on the client removes the token from localStorage, and the server then revokes it automatically
re2e20.explanation: If a token stays valid until exp, a stolen token works even after logout. This is worth discussing with the team as a risk.

zkf7wd.text: Why is cursor pagination better than offset/limit?
options: It lets you jump to an arbitrary page by number and show the total number of pages without an extra request
No better, but cursor pagination is simpler to test, because it has no limit parameter
It is simpler to implement and lets you jump to an arbitrary page by number
It is stable when new records are inserted: it doesn't duplicate or lose items between pages, and it is faster on large tables
zkf7wd.explanation: Test for offset: get page 1, add a record, get page 2 and check for duplicates at the boundary.

1b1bhez.text: What negative cases are there for the `limit` parameter?
options: Only a valid value within the limit
Only a missing value: the server must return the default number of items
0, negative, non-numeric, fractional, above the maximum, missing (the default)
Only the maximum and minimum from the documentation, the server handles the rest itself
1b1bhez.explanation: Expected is 400 with an explanation or clamping to the maximum, but definitely not a 500 and not returning the whole table.

14j0nl1.text: Why version an API, for example `/v1/`?
options: For performance: the server caches responses separately for each version and serves them without processing
To change the contract without breaking existing clients
For caching
For performance: the server caches responses separately for each version
14j0nl1.explanation: Breaking changes: removing a field, changing a type, a new required field in the request. Adding an optional field to a response usually doesn't break clients.

15esy22.text: Which API change is a breaking change?
options: An optional query parameter currency was added for filtering
The amount field in the response changed type from number to string
A new endpoint /v1/accounts/export was added for reports
A new optional field currency was added to the response
15esy22.explanation: A client doing `amount + fee` gets a concatenated string instead of a sum. A response schema in tests catches this immediately.

1os1qt1.text: What does the OpenAPI (Swagger) specification describe?
options: Server logs with examples of real requests and responses for each endpoint
Test cases for QA with expected results for each endpoint
Only a UI for manual API requests without schema descriptions
The API contract: endpoints, parameters, request and response schemas, status codes, authorisation
1os1qt1.explanation: From it you generate clients, mocks and checks that responses match the schema.

a4hour.text: How is GraphQL different from REST from the testing point of view?
options: GraphQL has no schema, so responses are checked only by the status code
GraphQL doesn't support authorisation and pagination, so tests are limited to checking the response schema
One endpoint, the client picks the fields; errors often arrive with 200 in an errors array, so the status code is not enough
It is tested the same way by status codes, because GraphQL returns 400 on any error in a request or resolver
a4hour.explanation: Extra risks: deeply nested queries (DoS), field-level authorisation, introspection in production.

1akpqcv.text: How do you test a webhook from a payment provider?
options: Only check that the endpoint answers 200 to the provider's test payload
Check the signature (HMAC), idempotent handling of repeated deliveries, the order of events and a 2xx response, as well as an invalid signature
Through the UI: pay a test order on the test environment and check that the order status changed to "Paid"
Webhooks aren't tested: the provider guarantees delivery, and our service only logs the received events
1akpqcv.explanation: Providers retry delivery on a timeout, so the same payment.succeeded can arrive twice.

12573dk.text: How should a client retry requests on 503?
options: Never retry 503, because a retry only increases the load on a service that is already unavailable
Immediately, in an infinite loop until a successful response
A limited number of attempts with exponential backoff and jitter, honouring Retry-After, and only for idempotent operations or with an Idempotency-Key
Retry any POST without limits and delays until a successful response, because 503 means the request was definitely not processed
12573dk.explanation: Jitter spreads the retries of different clients over time, so as not to create a wave of requests after the service recovers.

options: An authorisation format where the token is passed in links
A protocol for caching hypermedia responses at the CDN level
The response contains links to the allowed next actions on the resource
A pagination type with links to the first and last pages
1lnaok1.explanation: In practice it is rarely implemented fully, but the question sometimes comes up in interviews about REST.

options: Performance testing of contractual SLAs between services
The consumer describes its expectations of the API, and the provider verifies that it meets them, without a full e2e environment
Tests written only by the backend team to check their own code before a release
Checking the legal SLA contract between the consumer companies and API suppliers
czor7k.explanation: It catches breaking changes between microservices earlier than an integration environment.

1rujopf.text: Why use a mock server when testing an API client?
options: To reproduce responses that are hard to get from the real service: errors, timeouts, boundary data
To speed up production by replacing slow services with mocks
To store the client's request logs for analysis after a run
To replace all integration tests, because a mock fully reproduces the service
1rujopf.explanation: The risk: the mock drifts from reality. So mocks are best generated from the specification or verified with contract tests.

options: Generates Postman collections from an OpenAPI specification
Mocks a Postman server for local tests
Runs Postman collections from the command line, including on CI, with reporters
Encrypts the requests of Postman collections before sending them on CI
ozudaq.explanation: A non-zero exit code when tests fail stops the pipeline.

1l8ptty.text: Where is it best to keep a token obtained at login in a Postman collection?
options: In the request name, so the token is visible in the Collection Runner
In each request's body by hand or in the initial value, so the whole team sees it
In the current value of an environment variable via a script, without committing the value to the shared collection
In the initial value of a collection variable, so the whole team sees the token and doesn't have to log in
1l8ptty.explanation: The initial value is synced with the team, and the current value stays local.

c3qkbi.text: How do you run one Postman request with different data 20 times?
options: Postman doesn't support data-driven runs, so the data is changed by hand in each iteration
Copy the request 20 times and change the data in each
Collection Runner or Newman with a CSV/JSON data file and `pm.iterationData`
Only through a Pre-request loop with pm.sendRequest, because the Runner doesn't support data from files
c3qkbi.explanation: An expectedStatus column in the CSV lets you check both positive and negative cases in one run.

13yur2l.text: What does this Postman test check?
options: That the request ran 500 times without errors
That the response body is smaller than 500 bytes
That the response status is below 500, that is, there is no server error
That the response time is below 500 ms
13yur2l.explanation: A useful rough check, but not a replacement for load testing: one request from an office says nothing about p95 under load.

1wmg33w.text: What does p95 latency = 400 ms mean?
options: 95% of requests completed in 400 ms or faster, and 5% slower
95 requests completed in 400 ms in total
A maximum response time of 400 ms for 95 requests per minute
An average response time of 400 ms among 95 requests
1wmg33w.explanation: The average hides the slow tail. For SLAs you usually look at p95 and p99.

1p63vu6.text: How is load testing different from stress testing?
options: Load: above the limit, to find the breaking point. Stress: the expected load and SLAs
Stress is faster and shorter, and load lasts several hours with the same load
Load: the expected load, whether we meet the SLA. Stress: above the limit, to find the breaking point and the behaviour at it
Load is tested only for the UI in a browser, and stress only for the API with JMeter, so they don't overlap in tools
1p63vu6.explanation: There is also soak (a long-running load, looking for memory leaks) and spike (a sudden jump).

gz13im.text: Which tools are used for load testing an API?
options: Playwright
k6, JMeter, Gatling, Locust
Postman Collection Runner as the main one
Swagger UI
gz13im.explanation: Collection Runner runs requests sequentially and doesn't give a realistic load.

aiqg24.text: How do you test the idempotency of a transfer at the API level?
options: Send two identical POSTs in parallel with one Idempotency-Key and check: one operation in the DB, both responses identical, the balance debited once
Check only the status code of the second request: if it is 409, idempotency works and there is no need to check the balance in the database
Send two requests with different keys and check that the second operation is rejected as a duplicate
Send one request and check that the response contains the Idempotency-Key
aiqg24.explanation: Parallelism matters: sequential repeats often pass, while a race of two simultaneous requests breaks a naive implementation.

dqyekj.text: What is a client-side timeout and why is it important in integration tests?
options: A limit on the number of requests the client may send per minute before the server blocks it
The token's lifetime, after which the client must log in again
A delay before a retry, which the client increases after every failed attempt
The maximum time to wait for a response; without it a hung provider blocks the thread and the test hangs until the global timeout
dqyekj.explanation: Test: the provider responds in 60 s (a mock with a delay), and our service must return a controlled error within its own timeout.

1w4bthn.text: Which of these is a data leak in an API?
options: The response contains the id and email of the user making the request
The GET /users/me response contains passwordHash and internal fields
The response has an ETag header from which the resource version can be determined
The response contains the email and name of the account owner
1w4bthn.explanation: OWASP API: excessive data exposure. The front end doesn't show them, but they are visible in Network.

1khroyu.text: Why is a stack trace in the body of a 500 response considered a defect?
options: It slows the response down and increases the body size
It breaks the JSON and increases the response size
It reveals the internal structure: library versions, paths, DB queries, and helps attackers
It is not a defect: a stack trace helps developers find the cause of the error faster
1khroyu.explanation: The user must get a generic message and a correlation id, and the details must go to the server logs.

1xiigob.text: How do you test rate limiting on login?
options: Send a series of failed attempts and make sure that after the limit a 429 or a block comes, and that a successful login after a pause works again
Check only the UI message about a wrong password after three attempts
One failed login and a check of the error message
Rate limiting isn't tested functionally: it is an infrastructure setting, and only DevOps checks it in the gateway configuration
1xiigob.explanation: Also: the limit must work at the account and IP level, and the messages must not reveal whether an account exists.

1oz8s1i.text: What is SSRF in the context of an API?
options: Stealing a cookie through a forged request from another site
The server, by a parameter from the request, itself calls a given URL, and an attacker makes it reach into the internal network
SQL injection through a URL parameter in a request to the server, changing the query to the database
Forging a request from the user's browser to another site with their cookies
1oz8s1i.explanation: Risky endpoints: loading an avatar by URL, a webhook URL, importing a file by link. Test: the addresses 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, internal hosts.

zrod5t.text: Why is the message "A user with this email does not exist" on login considered a problem?
options: It isn't a problem: this way the user understands faster that they made a mistake in the email
It is badly translated and doesn't follow UX text guidelines
It returns the wrong status 404 instead of 401
It lets someone find out by brute force which emails are registered (user enumeration)
zrod5t.explanation: The same message and the same response time for a wrong email and a wrong password.

hjtckv.text: The interviewer gives the task "design a test framework". Where is it best for the candidate to start?
options: Name the tools: Playwright, Allure and GitHub Actions
Write the first login test to show their code style
Draw the folder structure and a basic Page Object
Clarify the requirements: test volume, time target, environments
hjtckv.explanation: Design starts with requirements and constraints. Choosing tools without understanding the scale and goals is not design but picking a library.

u8nbjh.text: The interviewer says: "There are no numbers, decide yourself". What is best to do?
options: Give an answer without numbers, describing only the layers
State the assumptions out loud and calculate from them
Ask for a test assignment with real data
Refuse to calculate, because there is not enough data
u8nbjh.explanation: Explicit assumptions make the calculations transparent, and the interviewer can adjust them. An answer without numbers doesn't show an understanding of scale.

e6pyyl.text: Which block most logically ends an answer following the scheme "requirements, layers, solution, trade-offs, ..."?
options: An estimate of the QA team's salaries
Success metrics of the solution
A list of all possible tools
A detailed code migration plan
e6pyyl.explanation: Metrics show how you will know the solution works: pipeline time, flaky rate, escaped defects.

1gbexzc.text: Which phrase best shows senior-level thinking in a payments task?
options: "First we automate all the manual test cases in a row"
"We will cover every button on the page with e2e tests"
"Let's take the most popular reporting tool"
"A repeated request must not create a second debit"
1gbexzc.explanation: For fintech the key risk is a double charge. Thinking about idempotency shows a focus on business risk, not on tools.

1c6zpvr.text: Why move locators and page actions into a Page Object?
options: So that reports are generated automatically
So that tests run in parallel
So that a UI change is fixed in one place
So that Playwright doesn't need locators
1c6zpvr.explanation: A Page Object isolates UI details. When the markup changes, one class is fixed, not hundreds of tests.

4hmn5d.text: Before an e2e transfer test you need a verified user with a balance. What is the best way to prepare one?
options: Take a shared user from the settings
Through the UI: registration, KYC and a top-up
Through the API or a test hook in a fixture
Write rows directly into the production DB
4hmn5d.explanation: Preconditions through the API are faster and more stable than through the UI. Use the UI only for what the test actually verifies.

k479i9.text: 2000 e2e tests of 20 seconds each must finish in 15 minutes (about 3 minutes of which is overhead). How many parallel slots are needed at minimum?
options: About 8-10
About 130-140
About 56-60
About 15-20
k479i9.explanation: 2000 x 20 s = 40,000 s, roughly 667 minutes. With 12 minutes for the tests: 667 / 12 = about 56 slots.

186wez5.text: The team suggests solving a slow e2e suite by buying 10 more CI machines. What will a Senior QA suggest considering first?
options: Run e2e only before a release once a month
Switch to sequential runs for stability
Raise `retries` to 3 to get rid of failures
Move some of the checks to the API level
186wez5.explanation: Many e2e tests verify logic that can be checked faster and more reliably at the API. Reviewing the pyramid often gives more than new machines.

1y0jyl6.text: Five product teams write tests. How do you organise the shared framework code?
options: A separate core package with versions, tests in the teams
One repository that only the QA team commits to
A copy of the framework in each team without synchronisation
No shared code: each test initialises everything itself
1y0jyl6.explanation: A shared core (clients, fixtures, config) evolves centrally, while the teams keep their own tests and don't block each other.

1gm0otk.text: Why shouldn't a test be built on data created by another test?
options: Playwright forbids access to other tests' data
Such data is automatically deleted after every test
It slows down HTML report generation
It creates an order dependency, and parallel runs break
1gm0otk.explanation: Dependence between tests makes them brittle: a different order or a parallel run gives failures.

1qds9b1.text: Transfer tests on 64 workers sometimes see an unexpected balance. They all use the account test_user_1. Which solution is the most correct?
options: Add `waitForTimeout(2000)` before the check
Raise `retries` to three for these tests
Separate accounts per test or per worker
Reduce the number of workers to two
1qds9b1.explanation: The cause is shared state. Delays and retries only mask the conflict, and cutting workers kills speed.

mgzoty.text: Creating an account takes 5 seconds. How do you keep isolation and not lose time in every test?
options: A worker-scoped fixture with a pool of accounts per worker
A test-scoped fixture that creates an account in every test
One account for the whole run, shared by all shards
A global setup that cleans the DB before every test
mgzoty.explanation: A worker-scoped fixture creates data once per worker. Workers don't overlap, and a test doesn't pay for creation every time.

13xe9ip.text: The provider's payment sandbox is unstable and can't reproduce timeouts. Which strategy is best?
options: All tests only through the sandbox, ignore failures
Test payment only in production with real cards
Don't test the provider integration at all
A stub for most tests, the sandbox separately
13xe9ip.explanation: A controllable stub gives stability and lets you reproduce errors and timeouts. A small suite with the real sandbox checks the actual integration.

bck2mp.text: What does the `--shard=2/4` flag do in Playwright?
options: Runs tests in two browsers out of four
Repeats each test twice out of four attempts
Runs the second of four parts of the suite
Runs tests in two workers out of four
bck2mp.explanation: Sharding splits the suite between machines. Each machine runs its own part, and the reports are merged afterwards.

1y9p4y8.text: The suite is split into 8 shards, but one shard takes 14 minutes while the others take 5-6. One file has 200 tests. What is most likely to help?
options: Increase the number of shards to 16
Add `retries: 2` to the config
Turn on `fullyParallel: true`
Set `workers: 1` on each shard
1y9p4y8.explanation: Without fullyParallel the tests of one file run sequentially in one worker. With it, distribution happens at the level of individual tests.

6b3zdy.text: How do you get one HTML report after a run on 8 shards?
options: The JUnit reporter, because HTML doesn't support sharding
The blob reporter on the shards and `merge-reports` in a separate job
Run all shards in one job without artifacts
The HTML reporter on every shard and copying the folders together
6b3zdy.explanation: Blob reports from every shard are uploaded to one job, where `npx playwright merge-reports` builds the final report.

e67m6l.text: What is a quality gate in CI/CD?
options: A separate server for running e2e tests
Manual release approval from QA
A rule that blocks a merge or a deploy
A code coverage report for management
e67m6l.explanation: A gate is an automatic condition: for example, all API tests and smoke must be green, otherwise the merge is impossible.

rgxcqb.text: After increasing shards from 8 to 16 the run time didn't change, and there are more timeouts. What is most likely?
options: Blob reports became too large to merge
The CI provider limits the number of artifacts
Playwright doesn't support more than 8 shards
The bottleneck is the shared test environment
rgxcqb.explanation: If staging can't take the load, more parallel clients only give timeouts. First find the bottleneck.

options: One that takes longer than 60 seconds
One that always fails after changes in the product
One that has no `expect` check at all
One that sometimes passes and sometimes fails on the same code
132xa73.explanation: Flaky means an unstable result without changes in the code. A test that fails consistently is simply red.

jvfgpm.text: A test checks the balance text right after a transfer and sometimes fails. What should you fix first?
options: Use a web-first assertion with waiting
Add a fixed `waitForTimeout(5000)`
Mark the test as `test.skip` until the release
Move the check into a separate test
jvfgpm.explanation: `await expect(locator).toHaveText(...)` repeats the check until the timeout. A fixed sleep is either too short or slows the suite down.

oxlf8z.text: A debit test fails about 1 time in 10 and passes on retry. What is the right reaction?
options: Move the test to nightly and stop analysing it
Raise `retries` to 3, because the test passes on repeat
Investigate the trace: it may be a race condition in the product
Delete the test, because it lowers trust in the pipeline
oxlf8z.explanation: Instability in a money scenario may be catching a real concurrency bug. A retry will hide it, and the bug will go to production.

1n8w3yq.text: What must a test that is moved to quarantine have?
options: A `test.only` mark in the file
A raised timeout of 5 minutes
An owner and a deadline for the fix
An `@smoke` tag for priority
1n8w3yq.explanation: Without an owner and a deadline, quarantine turns into a graveyard of tests that nobody brings back.

zrnusj.text: Why is an automatic step-level retry dangerous for POST /transfers?
options: Repeating a non-idempotent request may create a second transfer
A step retry turns off trace recording for the whole test
Playwright doesn't allow repeating POST requests in tests
POST requests always return the same response
zrnusj.explanation: A POST without an idempotency key is not idempotent. A retry after a timeout may create another debit.

50npv.text: What does the setting `trace: 'on-first-retry'` give you?
options: The test is repeated until the trace is clean
A trace is recorded for every test in the suite
The trace is deleted after the first successful run
A trace is recorded on the first retry of a failed test
50npv.explanation: The mode saves space: a trace is written only when a test failed and is being retried.

1tav0jj.text: The average pipeline time is 10 minutes, but developers complain about slowness. Which metric is worth looking at?
options: The p95 of pipeline time
The number of commits per day
Unit test code coverage
The number of tests in the suite
1tav0jj.explanation: The average hides the tail. p95 shows how long the worst runs are, which is what developers feel.

13d5ii7.text: Why should a test pass its own correlation id in API requests?
options: So that the response is cached separately for tests
To bypass rate limiting in the test environment
To find the logs of this request across all services
So that the server processes the request with higher priority
13d5ii7.explanation: A correlation id passes through the services and lets you quickly collect the logs of a specific failure.

1c258a6.text: Which metric most honestly shows the effectiveness of a test system for the business?
options: The number of test cases in the TMS
The total number of automated tests in the repository
The percentage of code line coverage
Escaped defects: bugs found in production
1c258a6.explanation: The number of tests and coverage can be grown without benefit. Bugs in production directly show what the test system missed.

rzmusk.text: What is the main job of a load balancer?
options: Store user sessions in its memory
Cache database responses for reads
Turn HTTP requests into queue messages
Distribute requests between instances of a service
rzmusk.explanation: An LB distributes traffic and, through health checks, removes unhealthy instances.

wl45ag.text: A user created a transfer, but the history page doesn't show it for another 1-2 seconds. The history is read from a replica. What is this?
options: A DB deadlock
Cache stampede
An index error
Replication lag
wl45ag.explanation: Asynchronous replication lags behind the primary. A read from a replica right after a write may not see the new data.

2byagr.text: A queue gives an at-least-once guarantee. What does that mean for a consumer that credits money?
options: It must be idempotent, because duplicates are possible
It must handle messages strictly one at a time
It may skip duplicate checks, the queue discards them
It receives every message exactly once
2byagr.explanation: At-least-once means repeated deliveries are possible. An idempotent consumer guarantees a single credit.

1y4uphp.text: After introducing a cache, a user sometimes sees another user's balance. What is the most likely cause?
options: The database has no index on the balance
The cache TTL is set too short
The cache key doesn't contain the user id
The cache works in write-through mode
1y4uphp.explanation: If the key doesn't take the user into account, different users get the same entry. That is a security incident, not just stale data.

1rtt65w.text: What is a DLQ (dead letter queue) for?
options: For messages that couldn't be processed after N attempts
For storing copies of all messages in case of an audit
For messages that the consumer has already processed successfully
For messages with the highest processing priority
1rtt65w.explanation: A DLQ stops a poison message from blocking the queue. In fintech these messages must be monitored, because they are money stuck in limbo.

1mfnh14.text: What does a contract test between two services verify?
options: That both services use the same database
That the producer and the consumer understand the API the same way
That the UI displays the data of both services correctly
That both services withstand peak load
1mfnh14.explanation: The contract records requests and responses. The producer checks in its own CI that it doesn't break the consumer's expectations.

tkck0t.text: What is a component test for a microservice?
options: A full e2e through all services on a shared staging
Checking a UI component in Storybook
The service through its API, a real DB, neighbours are stubs
A test of one service function with no DB and no network
tkck0t.explanation: A component test isolates the service: its DB is real (for example in Testcontainers), and its dependencies are replaced by stubs.

nay9oq.text: A transfer is asynchronous: the status is first `PENDING`, then `COMPLETED`. How should an e2e test check the result?
options: A fixed 30-second pause, then one check
Check only the `PENDING` status and finish
Immediately check `COMPLETED` in the POST response
Poll the status with a timeout matching the SLA
nay9oq.explanation: `expect.poll` or `toPass` wait for the final state. A timeout set by the SLA catches both an error and a speed degradation.

zo8zs7.text: In an order saga "reserve, pay, deliver" creating the delivery failed. What should the test check?
options: That the order stayed in the payment status
That the delivery was created on the second attempt
That the money was refunded and the reservation released
That the payment went through, the rest doesn't matter
zo8zs7.explanation: A saga replaces a distributed transaction with compensations. The final state must be consistent, with no half-finished operations.

1ygpild.text: What response does an API usually return when a client exceeds the rate limit?
options: `403 Forbidden`
`503 Service Unavailable`
`409 Conflict`
`429 Too Many Requests`
1ygpild.explanation: 429 is the standard status for exceeding a limit, often together with the `Retry-After` header.

i97nb4.text: A client repeated a payment POST with the same idempotency key and the same body. What is the expected behaviour?
options: The server returns `500` because of the duplicate key
A new payment with a new id is created
The result of the first payment is returned
The previous payment is cancelled and created again
i97nb4.explanation: An idempotency key lets you safely repeat a request: the server returns the stored result without a new debit.

n2dypy.text: Which type of load test looks for memory and connection leaks?
options: Smoke test
Spike test
Stress test
Soak test
n2dypy.explanation: Soak is a long-running load over hours that reveals gradual degradation of resources.

158g5v3.text: During a network partition the ledger is unavailable. How should the balance API behave under CAP if CP is chosen?
options: Accept debits and synchronise later
Return the last balance from the cache without a marker
Return an error instead of a stale balance
Return a zero balance until recovery
158g5v3.explanation: CP chooses consistency: better to refuse than to serve inconsistent data about money.

5lgjpb.text: What main problem does the Page Object Model solve?
options: A changed locator is fixed in one place
Tests run faster thanks to locator caching
Playwright itself generates a report for each page
Tests stop depending on auto-waiting
5lgjpb.explanation: POM encapsulates a page's locators and actions, so a UI change is fixed in one class, and tests read like a business scenario. The pattern doesn't affect speed or auto-waiting.

118tm1e.text: A test creates `LoginPage` before calling `page.goto()`. What happens to the locators from the constructor?
options: Nothing bad: the search happens only at the action
The test fails, because the button isn't in the DOM yet
Playwright throws a detached element error
The locator caches an empty search result
118tm1e.explanation: A `Locator` in Playwright is lazy: it only describes how to find an element. The search and auto-waiting happen at the moment of `click()`, so creating locators in the constructor is safe.

mk3gpi.text: Which approach to assertions in a Page Object is most often considered a compromise in Playwright projects?
options: All checks in the PO, the test only calls verify methods
Business checks in the test, only state waits in the PO
Checks in the PO, and the test only catches exceptions
No expect in the PO at all, not even waiting for load
mk3gpi.explanation: Business assertions in the test show the purpose of the scenario. Methods like `expectLoaded()` in the PO are acceptable, because they synchronise with the page state rather than verify a requirement.

ecjzfl.text: The check in this code sometimes fails even though the error appears on screen. Why?
options: `toBe` compares boolean values incorrectly
`isVisible()` returns a Promise that never resolves
`isVisible()` doesn't wait, the state is checked once
The `error` locator must be created inside the method itself
ecjzfl.explanation: `isVisible()` returns the current state without waiting. If the error appears after 200 ms, we get false. The right way is to give the test the locator and write `await expect(loginPage.error).toBeVisible()` with auto-retry.

6ne3yr.text: What does a Page Component usually take in its constructor?
options: The root Locator of its block
A string with a CSS selector of the whole page
A Browser object for a new context
An instance of the parent Page Object
6ne3yr.explanation: A component builds all its inner locators from the root. So one class works on any page and even several times on one.

a6tidf.text: A page has two tables: active and archived payments. How is it best to describe them in a Page Object?
options: One instance with the table index in every method
The locators of both tables directly in the page class
Two instances of the component with different roots
Two subclasses of DataTable, one for each table
a6tidf.explanation: A component takes a root locator, so it is enough to create `new DataTable(page.getByTestId('active'))` and `new DataTable(page.getByTestId('archived'))`. Subclasses and indexes only complicate the code.

4z4omn.text: `BasePage` has a header and a menu, and all pages inherit it. A login page without a header was added. What is the problem?
options: Playwright doesn't support inheritance in Page Objects
The page gets elements that aren't on it
The header is searched every time and noticeably slows tests down
TypeScript doesn't allow inheriting classes with locators
4z4omn.explanation: Inheritance imposes the same set of elements on all pages. Composition (a page has a `header` field) lets you take only the components that actually exist.

1l96jkl.text: The component is created for the active payments table, but the page also has an archived table. What will `rows()` return?
options: A strict mode error right at the call
The rows of only the first table in the DOM
An empty result, because root isn't used
The rows of both tables on the page
1l96jkl.explanation: The locator is built from `page`, not from `root`, so the scoping is lost. Strict mode fires only when acting on a single element, not when creating a locator. The right way: `this.root.getByRole('row')`.

9jgfw0.text: What does the code before and after the `use` call mean in a fixture?
options: The code after `use` runs only on failure
Before `use` is setup, after `use` is teardown
The code after `use` doesn't run automatically
The code before `use` runs only in worker scope
9jgfw0.explanation: A fixture prepares a resource, hands it to the test through `use`, and when the test finishes runs the code after `use`. Teardown runs even if the test fails.

j6h3ao.text: The fixture `paymentsPage` is declared with `test.extend`, but the test doesn't request it in its arguments. Will it be created?
options: No, only if scope test is not specified
No, a fixture is created only on request
Yes, but only for the worker's first test
Yes, all fixtures from extend are always created
j6h3ao.explanation: Fixtures are lazy: the runner creates only those that a test requested directly or through other fixtures. The exception is `{ auto: true }`.

options: An error: a worker fixture can't depend on `page`
The error appears only with more than one worker
It works, `page` becomes shared across the whole worker
It works, but `page` is created for each test
sbgcd3.explanation: `page` has test scope, and a worker fixture lives longer than a test, so Playwright forbids such a dependency. For a worker fixture you can use `browser` and create your own context.

31vdu8.text: Why are fixtures in Playwright Test considered better than a `BaseTest` base class with `beforeEach`?
options: TypeScript tests don't support base classes
Fixtures run in a separate process from the test
Laziness, isolation and guaranteed teardown
Fixtures cache their result between runs
31vdu8.explanation: A fixture is created only for a test that needs it, gives each test its own instances and always cleans up after itself. Fixtures also combine through `extend` and `mergeTests`.

1f0fps5.text: What is a fixture with `{ auto: true }` appropriate for?
options: Opening the needed page instead of goto
Collecting console errors in every test
Initialising all of the project's Page Objects
Creating test data for each scenario
1f0fps5.explanation: An auto fixture runs for every test without being requested. That suits cross-cutting things such as logging. Data, navigation and pages should be explicit dependencies of a test.

1up9ig5.text: What is the main idea of a Test Data Builder?
options: Keep test data in the framework's JSON files
Valid defaults, and the test changes only the important fields
Generate all the fields randomly for each test
Create all the data in the DB before the tests run
1up9ig5.explanation: A builder gives a valid object by default, and the test explicitly sets only what matters for the scenario. A new required field is added in one place.

options: A TypeError because of the repeated call to build
0, because p1 and p2 are the same object
undefined, because withAmount resets the data
100, because build returns a new object
1jnrybj.explanation: `build()` returns a reference to the internal `data`, so later changes to the builder mutate the already issued object. The right way is to return a copy: `return { ...this.data }`.

80gkp6.text: A test checks a fee of 1% of the payment amount, and faker generates the amount. What is the main problem?
options: faker gives the same values in all workers
The amount from faker will always be an integer
faker can't be used with Playwright Test
A failure is hard to reproduce, because the amount is different each time
80gkp6.explanation: Values that the check depends on are better set explicitly. faker is fine for unique fields like email, and for reproduction you should log the data or use `faker.seed()`.

rvcfk2.text: Tests run with `workers: 4`. What happens to the users' emails?
options: Within a worker all tests get the same email
Each `build()` call gives a new email
faker throws an error on static initialisation
All four workers get the same email
rvcfk2.explanation: A static field is evaluated once when the module loads, and the module is loaded separately in every worker. So the email is the same within a worker but different between workers, and registration will fail on a duplicate.

1enpqsx.text: Why is `Partial` used in the factory `createCard(overrides: Partial<Card> = {})`?
options: So that fields become readonly after creation
So that TypeScript doesn't check field types
So that the result has no required fields
So that you pass only the fields you need to change
1enpqsx.explanation: `Partial<Card>` makes all fields optional only for the argument. Defaults fill in the rest, and TypeScript still checks the types of the passed fields.

options: 'TEST USER', spread skips undefined
An empty string instead of undefined
A compile error under any settings
undefined, spread overwrote the default
hv62st.explanation: Spread copies a property even if its value is `undefined`. By default TS allows this (`exactOptionalPropertyTypes` can forbid it). Filter out undefined or don't pass such fields.

1shby7k.text: When is a Builder more appropriate than a simple factory function?
options: A complex object with many domain variations
An object with two fields and no variations
The object is used in only one test
Data has to be read from a CSV file before the test
1shby7k.explanation: A builder is justified when there are many variations and they are convenient to express as methods like `failed()`. For simple objects a factory with `Partial` is shorter and just as type-safe.

47fc17.text: A factory returns the exported object `DEFAULT_USER` without copying it. One test does `user.email = 'x@test.com'`. What happens?
options: Other tests in this worker see the changed email
Playwright reloads modules before every test
The change becomes visible in all workers of the run
`export const` forbids changing the object's properties
47fc17.explanation: `const` protects only the reference, not the contents. The module is cached in the worker process, so the mutation leaks into the later tests of this worker. A factory should return a new object every time.

1cqy8kj.text: What does wrapping steps in `test.step` give you?
options: A separate browser context for the step
Grouping of actions in the report and the trace
Parallel running of the test's steps
Automatic retry of an individual step
1cqy8kj.explanation: `test.step` groups actions under a clear name in the HTML report and Trace Viewer. It gives no parallelism, separate retry or new context.

1g4okoz.text: In which situation should you NOT use a steps layer (Facade)?
options: The steps are needed as a precondition in many tests
The test verifies exactly the action the facade hides
The steps must be shown in the report through test.step
The scenario touches several Page Objects at once
1g4okoz.explanation: A facade is good for preconditions and repeated end-to-end paths. If the test is about form validation, it should work with the page directly so the check is visible.

17xie3g.text: 200 tests need a logged-in user, but login is not what is being checked. What is the best way to do it?
options: Keep one browser logged in as a singleton
Through the UI in the beforeEach of every test
Once in a setup project and storageState
Through the UI in globalSetup with a page variable
17xie3g.explanation: A setup project logs in once and saves the state to a file, and tests pick it up via `storageState`. Variables from globalSetup aren't available to tests, and a shared browser breaks isolation.

4spssx.text: What does the `{ box: true }` option change in this step?
options: A step error doesn't stop the whole test
The step runs in an isolated context
The error points to the line that calls the step
The step isn't shown in the HTML report
4spssx.explanation: A boxed step hides the internal implementation at the place of the error: the report highlights the line where `sendMoney` was called. This is handy for business steps reused by many tests.

ufvkpm.text: What does the Strategy pattern describe?
options: Step-by-step construction of a complex object with defaults
One shared instance of a class for the whole process
Interchangeable algorithms behind one interface
A simplified interface to several different subsystems
ufvkpm.explanation: Strategy lets you swap an implementation (for example, login through the UI or the API) without changing the code that uses it. The other options describe Singleton, Builder and Facade.

18qfj6d.text: How is it most natural in Playwright Test to choose a strategy implementation for different config projects?
options: An option fixture with a value in projects
A module variable filled by globalSetup
A separate copy of the tests for each implementation
Inheriting the test class for the project
18qfj6d.explanation: A fixture with `{ option: true }` gets its value from `projects[].use` or `test.use`, and another fixture picks the strategy based on it. The test depends only on the result.

1p92yh8.text: A colleague suggests a `BrowserStrategy` with classes for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Your reaction?
options: Unnecessary, projects and devices already do this
Good, but better to combine it with a browser Singleton
Good, only that way will the tests become cross-browser
Unnecessary, because Playwright supports only Chromium
